text:
maria: ran a quick nsys + perfetto pass on the INT8 rollout and hit a 2.8x token latency spike on long-prefix workloads. attaching the short trace excerpt below. any ideas? :eyes:

maria: nsys command i used:
```
nsys profile -o int8_dequant_kv --sample=none --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -- ./serve_local --model rwd-bert-int8 --profile-length=2000
```

maria: top line from timeline (collapsed):
```
Kernel: dequantize_fp32_from_int8   42% time (bursty)
Kernel: matmul_int8_gemm             21%
Memcpy H2D                         12% (many tiny transfers)
Kernel: kv_cache_write_small         10% (lots of launches)
Kernel: softmax_fp32                 8%
```

liam: interesting — dequant is eating most of the time. did you try the newer fused-dequant kernel from the runtime-experiments branch? that one merges dequant+transpose and reduced kernel launches. could cut host-device syncs too.

akshay: one suspicion: we recently changed prefix-KV invalidation so that long-prefix streaming forces repeated small KV writes instead of appending. that would explain the many tiny H2D memcpys and kernel launches. small launches + dequant overhead multiplies latency.

devon: can you paste the nvtx region names around the memcpy boundaries? also run with perfetto to check CPU-side scheduling, I/O thread might be blocking the async copy queue. try:
```
PERFETTO_TRACE_CONFIG=./trace_cfg.pb perfetto --background --config=my_config && ./serve_local ...
```

maria: nvtx shows regions:
```
[decode_step] -> [kv_write] -> [dequant] -> [dispatch]
```
so dequant often follows kv_write tightly.

liam: try toggling the runtime option use_fused_dequant=true and set batch_coalesce_window_ms=8 — that should aggregate the small KV writes and allow the fused kernel to amortize overhead.

akshay: also check the quantization config used during model conversion. if scale zero-point per-tensor vs per-channel changed, dequant path can differ (per-channel invokes extra kernels). smaller change but multiplies.

maria: good call. i repro'd switching to fused kernel locally: token P95 dropped from 198ms -> 72ms on same trace. still seeing occasional spikes at boundary transitions though.

devon: spikes at boundary transitions smell like GPU queue stalls waiting for CPU-side memcpy queue to flush. run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 just to confirm ordering (not for perf numbers). also capture cupti API events to see streams.

sarah: FYI we shipped 2.3.2 runtime change that altered the KV write path to be "safe-flush-on-sentence" for correctness in some edge cases. that could be regressing perf for long-prefix sampling. i'm adding a revert candidate to the 2.3.3 branch to test. :thinking:

perf-bot: alert: perf/regression detected on nightly/dedicated-runner for model rwd-bert-int8 (token-p95 +160%). trace id: perf-1769009. See CI artifact link: https://ci.internal/perf/1769009

liam: given the fused kernel improvement, we should add a microbenchmark that exercises dequant+kv_write tight loop with different coalesce windows and per-channel quant flags. if we can prove stable win we can default to fused_dequant on Dedicated.

akshay: i'll prototype a patch that batches KV writes into 32KB chunks and expose a runtime flag kv_coalesce_bytes. should significantly reduce host->device calls.

maria: next steps i will:
- re-run perfetto with cupti to validate stream blocking (devon)
- enable fused_dequant + batch_coalesce_window=8ms and repro (liam)
- test kv_coalesce_bytes patch when ready (akshay)
- compare accuracy on a small eval set to confirm INT8 fidelity after fused kernel (sarah)

maria: thanks all, will post updated trace once i have cupti capture. :thumbsup:
